question: An investigator studying the immunologic profile of various cells notices that the blood of a test subject agglutinates upon addition of a serum containing antibodies against P blood group antigens. Infection with which of the following pathogens would most likely be prevented by these antibodies?
analysis: The presence of antibodies against P blood group antigens indicates that the test subject has anti-P antibodies. These antibodies are naturally occurring and can provide protection against certain pathogens that express P blood group antigens on their surface. Among the options provided, Babesia microti is a protozoan parasite that expresses P blood group antigens and can cause babesiosis. Therefore, the antibodies against P blood group antigens would most likely prevent infection with Babesia microti.
